Title: About Daily Work Sheet Logging
Content:
Daily Work Sheet Logging is a web-based operational data capture, compliance monitoring and management reporting application designed for Emergency & Dispatch Operations. It replaces fragmented paper or ad-hoc worksheet processes with a structured workflow for recording completed field jobs, validating key data points and turning daily crew activity into actionable performance information.

## Purpose
The application is intended to improve visibility, consistency and accountability in the daily job-completion process. It focuses on work actually completed during each crew shift rather than on daily assignment counts. The standard minimum job-completion target is read from the application Settings sheet and is currently configured at six completed jobs per crew/shift unless an authorized administrator changes that setting.

## What the application records
- Contractor, work type, date worked, parish/location, crew, team members and shift.
- Job ID, customer details, problem reported and action taken.
- Assigned, on-site and completed timestamps for each job.
- Materials used, voltage readings and remarks where applicable.
- Submission source, submitter, review status and audit information.

## Compliance and performance monitoring
The system evaluates production compliance against the configured completed-job target, checks required data-point completeness, validates chronological timestamp order and identifies unusually short timestamp gaps. It also calculates assignment-to-on-site, on-site-to-completion and assignment-to-completion durations and can flag configured duration overruns. These measures are presented separately so that job output, data quality and response performance are not reduced to a single unexplained score.

## Dashboard, reporting and insights
Authorized users can review KPI cards, crew and contractor performance, parish results, timing analysis, exceptions and filterable reports. CSV export is available for further analysis. The AI Insights panel is currently rules-based and deterministic; it summarizes trends from application data and does not send worksheet data to an external generative-AI service.

## Roles and access
Access is controlled using the active Google account and the role stored in the Users sheet. Admin users manage system configuration and master data. Superusers have broad operational reporting and review access. Contractor users are restricted to the functions and contractor data made available to their configured account. Actual access also depends on the Google Apps Script web-app deployment permissions selected by the application owner.

## Data and configuration
The application uses Google Sheets as its backend database and reads operational settings, users, contractors, crews, parishes, shifts, work types and legal/information content dynamically from the configured spreadsheet. When no database ID has been configured, the application can create its database automatically and store the Spreadsheet ID in Script Properties.

## Product attribution
Daily Work Sheet Logging was designed and developed by Qwik Business Solutions. Product names, organization names and third-party technologies referenced in the application remain the property of their respective owners.

## Version and evolution
The application is designed so that operational thresholds, master data and informational content can evolve without hardcoding routine business changes into the interface. Administrators should document configuration changes and validate them before relying on new thresholds or report outputs in production.

Title: Disclaimer & Operational Use Notice
Content:
Daily Work Sheet Logging is an operational administration, compliance-monitoring and management-reporting tool. It is intended to support informed review; it is not a substitute for professional judgment, official operating procedures, safety requirements or the organization's designated systems of record.

## Data accuracy and completeness
All dashboards, compliance percentages, time calculations, exception flags and reports depend on the accuracy, completeness and timing of the information submitted by users or imported from files. Incorrect Job IDs, omitted fields, inaccurate timestamps, duplicate records, wrong crew selections or incomplete worksheet data can produce misleading results. Users and supervisors remain responsible for verifying material information against appropriate source records.

## Official records take precedence
Where information in this application conflicts with an official operational, outage-management, work-management, financial, safety, HR or other designated system of record, the authorized source system and approved organizational process should be used to resolve the discrepancy. This application should not be used to overwrite or reinterpret official records without proper review.

## Compliance indicators are decision-support signals
The six-job target, 15-minute timestamp-gap rule, overrun thresholds, required fields, compliance weights and status thresholds are configurable business rules. A warning or compliant status indicates how the submitted data compares with the configured rules; it does not independently establish employee performance, misconduct, contractual breach, customer impact, safety compliance or the factual cause of an operational event.

## Time and duration calculations
Assignment-to-on-site, on-site-to-completion and assignment-to-completion values are calculated from submitted timestamps, including logic for shifts that cross midnight. These calculations cannot determine whether a timestamp was entered at the actual event time, entered retrospectively, affected by device/system delay or otherwise inaccurate. Exceptions should therefore be investigated before conclusions are drawn.

## AI Insights
The AI Insights feature in this version is a rules-based narrative generator. It summarizes metrics and trends already calculated by the application and does not constitute an independent investigation, prediction or expert opinion. It should be used as a prompt for review rather than as the sole basis for operational, disciplinary, contractual or financial decisions.

## Safety and operational decisions
Nothing in the application authorizes work, changes switching or safety procedures, replaces permits, bypasses dispatch instructions, alters escalation protocols or overrides applicable safety rules. Field and control-room personnel must continue to follow approved procedures, instructions and required safety controls.

## Availability and technical limitations
The application depends on Google Apps Script, Google Sheets, browser-based libraries, network availability, user permissions and third-party services. Temporary outages, quotas, permission changes, browser restrictions, spreadsheet edits or service changes may affect availability or functionality. Appropriate backups, access controls and recovery procedures should be maintained by the organization operating the deployment.

## Security and confidentiality
Users should access the application only through authorized accounts and should not share credentials or export sensitive information to unauthorized locations. Administrators are responsible for configuring deployment access, spreadsheet sharing, user roles and data-retention practices in accordance with organizational requirements.

## No warranty or professional advice
To the extent permitted by applicable agreements and law, the application is provided as a software tool without a guarantee that every result will be error-free, uninterrupted or suitable for every operational circumstance. Information displayed by the application is not legal, accounting, engineering, safety or other professional advice.

## Review responsibility
Material exceptions, unusually short or long durations, low job-completion results, incomplete records and apparent discrepancies should be reviewed with the relevant source records and personnel before action is taken.
